design.decision_rule: BLOCK iff the ticker's deal answer satisfies `deal_pins_price(a)`: `a.status == "signed"` AND ( (`a.role == "target"` AND `a.consideration in {"cash","mixed","unknown"}`) OR `a.role == "shell"` ). Everything else PASSES: role buyer / none, status proposed / speculation / completed / none, and a signed target paid in `stock` (the CSR label — an all-stock merger does not fix the price). Definitions the model is given and the code derives from: ROLE = this ticker's own part in a deal — `target` (another company is buying THIS company's shares; includes JBS-style minority buy-ins only when THIS ticker is the one being bought), `buyer` (this company buys another company, asset or a subsidiary's minority: FWDI, CHYM, JBS, SWKS, DFH, BANF, MAIR, ONDS), `shell` (this listed company is the vehicle of a reverse merger — a private company merges into it and its holders take control: SUNE 'definitive reverse merger with Suniva', CLRO 'merger agreement between [Vivani's] wholly owned subsidiary Cortigent and Nasdaq-listed ClearOne'), `none` (no deal involving this company's own shares: sector M&A commentary, a peer's deal, index inclusion, a funding agreement — RGTI, GPRK, IOVA, UMAC, SOUN). STATUS: `signed` = a definitive / merger agreement is signed by both boards, or a tender offer has commenced, with terms stated; `proposed` = unsolicited or non-binding proposal, letter of intent, bid received, 'in talks', 'exploring a sale / strategic alternatives' (WAY, HZO, RNW, PZZA, FRMI); `speculation` = rumours, 'potential takeover targets' lists, 'could pursue acquisitions', a denial (VKTX, IOVA headline, LCID, WEN, PYPL, IMAX); `completed` = the deal has closed (a ticker still trading after close was the buyer — ONDS, COCO); `none`. CONSIDERATION (what the TARGET's holders receive): `cash` = a stated cash price per share or 'all-cash' (ACVA $1.9B all-cash, DV $13.60, SYNA $123), `stock` = acquirer shares only / fixed exchange ratio / 'all-stock merger' (CSR), `mixed` = cash plus stock, `unknown` = a deal is described but terms are not in the text, `none`. 'Fixes its price' is therefore judged as: a signed deal whose consideration carries a stated cash value (cash or mixed) or whose terms are not stated (default pinned — operator decision 3); an all-stock deal does not pin. The `shell` arm exists ONLY to honour the two operator TP rulings (SUNE 07-04, CLRO 08-08) — without it CLRO reads as target/signed/stock and is indistinguishable from CSR (wrongly blocked), so the rule cannot separate the two rulings without a shell role; it is operator decision 1, not part of his recorded direction. The verdict is derived in code (`ma_filter.deal_pins_price`, pure, unit-tested); the model answers facts only. The audit row records role/status/consideration/counterparty on every block and every release so the monthly accuracy review shows WHY each decision was made.

design.replay_plan: Script: `scripts/probes/_692_replay_deal_question.py`, read-only on prod (`docker exec apollo-market python -m scripts.probes._692_replay_deal_question --cap 400`), run ONCE, every output to `scripts/probes/_692/replay_*.jsonl` (capture once, read many). Steps: (1) Load the population file (137 ticker-days) + the 13 veto rows + 4 ROKU acquirer-skips + the 07-04/08-08/07-12 labelled names not in the window → ~155 cases; build `cases.jsonl` with ticker, date, detector, old source, old verdict, label provenance. (2) Assemble each case's text per full_text_source (tier-shadow row ≥08-24 exact; EDGAR+Benzinga+Polygon rebuild <08-24 approximate; Polygon `on_or_before` for every case) → `replay_corpora.jsonl`, with an `exact|approximate` flag per case; $0 (Polygon/EDGAR within plan). (3) Classifier arm (EP cases, 97): run the NEW `_classify_catalyst_claude` (new schema + RULE 3) on the stored/rebuilt corpus once per case → quality + DealAnswer; ~3.5k input / 300 output tokens on claude-sonnet-5-5 ($2/$10) ≈ $0.010/call ≈ $1.0. (4) Headline arm (all 155 cases): candidate selection (unchanged keyword pre-filter + litigation skip + insights presence) over the re-fetched articles, ≤3 articles/case → `classify_deal_headline` ≈ 900/80 tokens ≈ $0.0026/call, ≤150 calls ≈ $0.4. (5) Stability: the 23 labelled cases × 3 runs × both arms ≈ 140 calls ≈ $0.9 — a labelled case whose verdict flips across runs fails the replay (a one-shot pass is not a verify for a stochastic model). (6) Apply `deal_pins_price` → per-case NEW verdict; emit `replay_results.jsonl` and a table: old verdict / new verdict / role / status / consideration / exact-or-approx / label. Hard cap: 400 model calls or $5, whichever first (the script counts tokens via `cost_for_call` and stops). Priced whole path up front: replay ≈ $2.5–3 one-time; ongoing run cost ≈ classifier +~40 output tokens × ~30 grades/day ≈ $0.01/day + headline question typical ≤2 calls/day ≈ $0.005/day (cap 40/day = $0.10/day worst) → under $3/month. Acceptance (the DoD): all ten 10-01 wrongly-blocked names PASS, ACVA/SUNE/CLRO BLOCK (SUNE/CLRO only under decision 1), the 07-04 and 08-08 FP names PASS, zero flips in the 3-run check; the released / still-blocked list goes to him for sign-off BEFORE deploy (THE LINE; CHANGE_PROCESS rule 3). Regression harness: `scripts/probes/_284_mna_acquirer_backtest.py` reshaped to (ticker, date, recorded DealAnswer fixture from the replay, expected verdict) → runs `deal_pins_price` deterministically at $0 and FAILS on today's code (FWDI: today `is_likely_ma(catalyst_quality='mna', texts)` → True) and PASSES on the fix; `--live` mode re-asks the model within the same cap for the labelled cases. PRE-REGISTERED EXPECT / DONE-WHEN for the deployed task (written now, before the data): BASELINE since Guard D (08-08, ~8 weeks): classifier 18 / polygon 6 / keyword 0 ticker-days ≈ 3 blocks/week, 10 of 11 wrong in September. EXPECT: `mna_filter_released` rows appear for buyer / proposal / no-deal names within the first week (the positive observable — alerts are NOT the signal, a released name may still fail grade/score); every `mna_filter_fired` row carries role ∈ {target, shell} + status = signed + consideration ≠ stock; blocks fall to ≤1/week. UNINTENDED, watched together: `mna_headline_unanswered` count (expect ≤2/week; a daily cap hit is a defect), `mna_grade_without_pin` count (expect ~0; >3/week means the prompt rule is not holding), `mna_deal_answers_conflict` count, classifier latency p90 unchanged. DONE-WHEN: 20 trading days with his monthly accuracy review labelling every block correct and no released name labelled a real target; the first wrong block or wrongly released real target reopens #692. WOULD-FAIL-IF: a `mna_filter_fired` row whose fields do not say target/shell + signed; a released name he later labels a real target; zero `mna_filter_released` rows in 10 trading days (the comparator or the release path is dead).
operator_decisions: 1. Reverse-merger shells (SUNE 06-08, CLRO 07-02): keep blocking under an explicit `shell` role? TODAY: blocked, ruled correct twice. CONFLICT: his recorded direction is 'target / buyer / none, block only on target + signed'; neither SUNE (surviving entity) nor CLRO (listed company a private subsidiary merged into) is a cash-pinned target, and without the shell role CLRO reads target/signed/stock — identical to CSR, which he labelled wrongly blocked — so the rule cannot honour both rulings. The $5 price floor is NOT a substitute: it exists on EP/low-cap/9m but not on the flag detector, and SUNE fired after passing 9m's own $5 check mid-run. His 07-04 SUNE reasoning was 'not a clean EP at $2.83', not price-pin. RECOMMENDATION: keep the shell rule (it preserves both rulings and names the real reason — a reverse-merger shell is not a clean EP), stated in the SSoT as a methodology rule riding on the M&A filter.

2. Mixed cash+stock consideration on a signed target: pinned? TODAY: blocked (any 'mna'). RECOMMENDATION: block — a stated per-share cash component anchors the price; SYNA shows the stock→cash flip changes the trade.

3. Signed target whose consideration is not in the text (`unknown`): block or pass? TODAY: blocked. RECOMMENDATION: block (default pinned unless the text says all-stock) — a signed acquisition of a public target is cash in the large majority of cases, and CSR was explicitly described as all-stock.

4. Headline question UNANSWERED (API error, truncation, daily cap, inside 9:30–9:45): block as today's keyword verdict would, or pass? TODAY: a keyword hit blocks. RECOMMENDATION: pass + `mna_headline_unanswered` audit row — the keyword verdict was 3 of 3 wrong in September, the flag path still has the price-signature backstop, and a truly pinned name rarely breaks the ORB high (10:00 unfilled-cancel). Implemented as runtime toggle `mna_headline_unanswered_blocks` set to his ruling.

5. Retie the `mna` GRADE to the pin verdict (grade 'mna' only when target/shell + signed + not stock; otherwise grade the catalyst on merit)? TODAY: 'mna' = any merger involvement → 0 points on the catalyst axis, lattice passthrough, allocator weight 0 — a released FWDI/CSR would be admitted and never alert. This is a grade change, so it is his. RECOMMENDATION: yes, retie — otherwise the release is cosmetic.

6. Sign-off on the replay's released / still-blocked list BEFORE deploy (already in #692's DoD; CHANGE_PROCESS rule 3 — the agent does not classify). The agent-read rows in regression_cases (SYNA, DV, UTZ, CRNX, FBRX, NUVL, DFH/BANF/MAIR, THR/CECO, ROKU) are his to label, not findings.
risks: Model variance on the proposed-vs-signed boundary (RNW's 'confirmatory letter', HZO's 'final round of bidding', NUVL's 'takeover bid at a premium'): a one-shot pass is not a verify — the 3-run stability check on the labelled cases gates ship; any flip → tighten the prompt wording before deploy, never after.

Agent-read volume estimates rest on the 200-char Perplexity `news_summary`, not the corpus the grader read (26 of 51 classifier blocks READ as earnings/no-deal text, but the 8-K the grader saw may say otherwise — e.g. FUL 06-29 8-K item 1.01): every such row is a replay input, not a finding; pre-08-24 EP corpora are rebuilt and approximate.

Sonnet 5.5 refusal class: both new prompts are verdict enums first with one short reasons field last and no 'reason first' wording; verify on the live model with 3+ real inputs (the 09-29 theme-stack lesson), not on a mock.

findings.summary: Grade 'mna' with no usable deal fields (fields missing, out of vocabulary, or cut off) now passes. The only trace is an mna_grade_without_pin audit row. Today, grade 'mna' blocks (Guard C aside). This failure-mode policy is not in the decisions table. A second case is also unlisted: grade 'mna' while the answered fields say no pin. The branch lets the fields decide, which is a recommendation applied as the default.
findings.fix: In is_likely_ma: when catalyst_quality == 'mna' and deal_answer is None, keep today's block (source 'claude_classifier_unanswered') and list it as decision 4b with today's behaviour (block). List the answered-but-contradictory case as its own decision, stating the branch's recommendation (fields decide). Until he rules on it, keep today's block there too, or state explicitly that it changes today.

findings.summary: The replay asks one question per ticker-day, but the live rule blocks when either the grader OR a headline pins. An EP day replayed on the classifier and reported 'released' can still be blocked in production by a headline candidate (headline_candidates_n > 0). The released / still-blocked list he signs could therefore be wrong, and that list is the sign-off. Also, rows before 2026-08-24 have no grounded_head, so SUNE (06-08) and CLRO (07-02) replay on a rebuilt corpus or the 200-char summary. A 'released' result for either would reflect thin text, not the rule. The pytest cases (test_mna_target_question_692.py lines 174-188) prove the rule only, using expected answers.
findings.fix: On EP days with headline_candidates_n > 0, ask both questions and combine them with the live OR rule. Re-price the whole run before the paid pass (adds about 1-3 calls per such day). On the sign-off page, mark SUNE and CLRO replay rows as thin-text, with the harness as their proof.

findings.summary: The new rule-3 prompt and the four extra required fields go into every EP grade, not only deal names. The grade feeds the score, which drives HIGH alerts and live ORB entries. The replay measures only the deal answer, so any grade shift on non-deal catalysts is unmeasured. That is a change touching THE LINE with no backtest evidence planned. Decision 5 covers re-tying the 'mna' grade, not this side effect.
findings.fix: Add a grade-stability check to the same paid run: re-grade a priced sample (around 30 recent non-deal rows from mi_catalyst_tier_shadow.grounded_head) with the old tool/prompt and the new one, and report quality flips. Price it with pricing_for alongside the replay, and put the flip count on the sign-off page.

findings.summary: The ORB-window skip applies to every caller, not only the EP scan it was built to protect. The low-cap lane is a detached task, and its row is fixed at the first qualifying post-open tick (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Its ma_flag is therefore set inside 9:31-9:45, where the headline question is never asked, so with OFF the lane's only catalyst check goes dark. Its telemetry also cannot tell 'answered: no deal' from 'unanswered'. The right fix depends on the decision-4 default.
findings.fix: Make the skip opt-in: add a skip_in_orb parameter to is_likely_ma that only _post_grade_filters sets. Alternatively, have the lane store ma_flag=NULL plus the unanswered reason when the scan comes back unanswered.

findings.summary: One 40-calls-a-day budget is shared across the whole process: EP pre-market, the low-cap lane after 9:45, the flag scan at 17:25 (gathered in parallel, 21-day lookback) and anticipation at 17:35 (up to 40 checks x 3 articles). Once it is spent, every later question is unanswered, which under OFF means pass. The cap saves almost nothing (about $0.005 a call), and the SSoT calls a cap hit a defect, but nothing alerts on it.
findings.fix: Reserve the budget for the EP path (per-caller budgets) or raise the cap to something like 400 a day. Send a Telegram on the first daily_cap hit each day. Do not let a shadow lane spend the money path's budget.

findings.summary: Only the 3 newest keyword-candidate articles are asked. Older candidates are dropped without being recorded as unanswered, so neither decision 4 nor any audit row covers them. Today the filter considered all 20 fetched articles. A target whose 3 newest candidates are bystander mentions is passed without a trace.
findings.fix: Add candidates beyond _HEADLINE_MAX_ARTICLES to scan.unanswered with why='article_cap' so the decision-4 knob covers them and they show up in audit. Alternatively, keep asking past answered no-pin articles until a pin is found or the per-day cap is reached.

findings.summary: Latency on the money path: in-window, the 9:31 path makes no new headline calls; the in-window legacy grade carries about 40-60 more output tokens. Pre-market ticks are the problem. Each EP candidate can wait on up to 3 headline calls in series (20 s timeout each, 60 s worst case) inside the sequential grading loop. The ORB guard is checked only when a call starts, so a call started at 9:29:5x runs into the window and can delay the 9:30/9:31 scans.
findings.fix: Ask the 3 or fewer articles at once (asyncio.gather) under one overall deadline. Treat a call as in-window when now + _HEADLINE_TIMEOUT_S would pass 9:30, or cap the timeout at the time left before 9:30.

findings.summary: The monthly review cannot see these passes. When every candidate went unanswered and the name passed, no mna_filter_released row is written (old_reasons only adds headline_keyword when scan.released is non-empty, and non-EP callers send no grade or texts). The monthly review reads only fired and released rows. A further gap: the comparator's grade_mna reason uses the new grade, which is now tied to the pin. A grader release with no keyword in the 200-char texts (FWDI's 'proposal to acquire' contains none) therefore writes no released row. That gives the 'zero released rows in 10 days' fail condition a false-alarm path.
findings.fix: Add mna_headline_unanswered rows where blocked=false to the review's under-fire section. In the comparator, add an old_reason whenever the grader answered a deal that does not pin (e.g. 'grader_deal_no_pin' when role != 'none'). Note the remaining blind spot in the pre-registration.

findings.summary: The /why deal line is not required by the design: it is display only and outside the filter, the classifier and the headline path. It is harmless, and agent.py is already loaded by the execution container, so it adds no deploy scope.
findings.fix: Keep it as is, or move it into its own commit so the THE LINE sign-off diff covers only the filter.

findings.summary: Three comments are now wrong. The lane docstring and the mi_lowcap_lane_signals column comment say is_likely_ma is 'keyword + Polygon headlines, no LLM'. The _post_grade_filters docstring says the per-tick re-run happens 'without any LLM call'. The headline question now makes a model call.
findings.fix: Update all three comments to describe the headline deal question: a model call, memoized per article per day, capped, skipped in the ORB window.

findings.summary: The replay asks only one path per ticker-day, but the new filter blocks if the grader's answer OR any of the 3 newest headline answers pins the price (a headline overrides the grader). So a PASS from the replay is only an upper bound, and its 'labelled acceptance' cannot show the DoD's 'releases all ten'. It skips the headline question on the 7 classifier releases (FWDI, CHYM, JBS, GPRK, WAY, CSR, SWKS), skips the grader on the 3 headline releases (IOVA, VKTX, RGTI, all EP days), and asks 1 article where production asks up to 3.
findings.fix: Before the one paid run: on every EP day ask the grader AND repeat headline_deal_scan (3 newest candidates, stop at the first pin); compute verdict = grader pins OR headline pins; keep both answers in the record. Headline days also take up to 3 candidates. Move the two test pins this breaks: tests/test_mna_replay_692.py:86 (MAX_CALLS == 200) and :194 (new_decision is None unless price_signature). Price the whole path from the $0 dry run's headline_candidates_n. The export has 151 ticker-days, 108 on EP (101 classifier + 7 headline). Worst case is about 530 calls x ~$0.011 = ~$5.9, over the $5 ceiling; the real count is lower and the dry run gives it for free.

findings.summary: The prompt defines 'signed' as 'definitive/merger agreement signed ... terms stated', but defines consideration 'unknown' as 'terms not in the text', and decision 3 blocks signed + unknown. A model following the text can put a signed deal with no stated terms under 'proposed' and release it. Both must-block texts state no terms: SUNE ('definitive reverse merger with Suniva') and CLRO (title only).
findings.fix: Drop ', terms stated' / 'with terms stated' from the signed definition in DEAL_FIELD_PROPERTIES and RULE 3; terms belong only to deal_consideration. Land this before the paid replay: the replay embeds the prompt word for word and the drift test forces the copy to match, so a later edit means paying for a second run.

findings.summary: Role 'target' reads 'another company is buying this company's shares', and 'none' reads 'no deal involving this company's own shares'. A signed PIPE (private share sale) or a strategic or government equity investment therefore fits target/signed/cash, which blocks. RGTI 09-08, one of the ten, was graded off an 8-K that carries item 3.02 (unregistered equity sale) next to the $100M Commerce agreement, and the replay never asks RGTI's grader (finding 1).
findings.fix: Define target as 'another company is acquiring all of / control of this company, so its holders are paid out'. Name minority stakes, PIPEs, private placements, government or strategic equity investments, warrants and buybacks as 'none', in the shared field description, RULE 3 and the headline prompt. Land it before the paid run.

findings.summary: Proposed operator decision 7, not a pure defect: any pinning headline overrides a grader that read the same deal with stated terms. Because 'unknown' pins (decision 3), a headline that states no terms (target/signed/unknown, e.g. an investigation-firm notice about the 'sale of Centerspace') would re-block CSR even when the grader read 'all-stock' from the 8-K. Every classifier-path case in the harness has zero Polygon articles, so this override is untested on the labelled names.
findings.fix: Add it to the sign-off table as decision 7. Today: the classifier path returned first and Polygon was never consulted. Recommendation: a headline overrides only when the grader found no deal or did not answer, or when the headline states cash/mixed; 'unknown' never overrides a grader's stated 'stock'. Add harness cases that give CSR, SWKS and CHYM realistic Polygon articles.

findings.summary: Decision 4's toggle ships OFF, meaning an unanswered headline lets the name through. That picks his decision for him and changes today's behaviour: today a keyword headline blocks. 'Unanswered' covers the 9:30-9:45 window (incl. the 9:31 ep_scan_open), the daily cap, the 20s timeout and the give-up after 2 failed attempts. On flag / low-cap lane / anticipation the headline is the only check, so for them an unanswered question means the filter is off.
findings.fix: Make his explicit ruling on decision 4 (and on 1, 2, 3, 5, plus 7 above) a recorded precondition of deploy, next to the released / still-blocked sign-off. Do not pick ON or OFF yourself. Keep 'today = keyword headline blocks' stated in the table.

findings.summary: The 40-calls/day cap was never measured. It is shared across the whole process, including the low-cap lane tick, which calls is_likely_ma(check_polygon=True) on every admitted name every 5 minutes alongside the EP scan, at up to 3 calls per ticker with a keyword article in 14-21 days. Once spent, every remaining question that ET day goes unanswered and passes.
findings.fix: Size the cap from a $0 count of keyword-candidate articles per day over a few past days' EP + low-cap lane + flag universes (Polygon fetch + _candidate_articles, no model), or reserve part of the budget for the EP scan. Include the expected daily_cap rate in EXPECT.

findings.summary: The fallback prefers the 200-character audit excerpt over the full stored text: `td.get("news_summary") or shadow.news_summary`. The audit excerpt is never empty, so the shadow table's full narrative (up to ~600 chars) is never read. The grader's own claude_analysis is selected but never used.
findings.fix: Use shadow news_summary first and append shadow claude_analysis; drop to the audit excerpt only when the shadow row is missing. Label the source in corpus_source.

findings.summary: The tests are real: they call the production is_likely_ma with only Polygon and the model faked. I reproduced the harness --old-module run against origin/main: all ten flip BLOCK->PASS, ACVA, SUNE and CLRO stay BLOCK, 14 flips, 0 labelled misses. But the ten release cases inject the EXPECTED answer, so they test deal_pins_price and the plumbing and cannot fail on a model or prompt regression. Lens 3 is clean: the note and analysis fields come last, and the reasoning-first guard covers agents/ and shared/.
findings.fix: After the replay, write each labelled case's recorded model answer into the harness fixtures in place of the expected answer, and list any case where the two differ, so the named regressions pin what the model actually said.

findings.summary: MODEL is hard-coded to claude-sonnet-5-5. Production asks GROUNDED_GRADE_MODEL, which a resolver picks (tier tracking + role holds), so on the box the replay could question a different model than the live filter would.
findings.fix: Import shared.llm_models.GROUNDED_GRADE_MODEL at run time, print it with the cost estimate, and abort if it differs from the id the drift test expects.

findings.summary: Lens 5 — the population shows real pinned names that the rule releases by design. These are not defects, but his sign-off list must name them. All-stock signed targets: LBRDA/LBRDK 06-29, whose price is tied to Charter's by a fixed exchange ratio, consistent with his CSR ruling. Take-privates still at the proposal stage: NUVL 06-09, HZO 08-10, RNW 08-11, PZZA 05-15. SYNA 10-02 (onsemi, signed, $123 cash) is an unlabelled name that must stay blocked. DSGN 05-18 and PD 05-29 were caught by the retired keyword path and now depend entirely on the grader's fields.
findings.fix: Add a MUST-SHOW set to the replay's stderr summary that prints these rows with old vs new verdict and the answer, for his labelling. Do not add them to LABELS: the agent does not label.
